# 1 Maccabees Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 5

---

## Council Notes

**On the division of command (vv.17-20):** The three-front strategy — Judas/Jonathan to Gilead, Simon to Galilee, Joseph/Azariah to hold Judea — mirrors the command structures of the judges period. The strict orders to Joseph and Azariah (*not* to engage independently) foreshadow their failure in vv.55-62.

**On "put them under the ban" / "utterly devoted them to destruction" (v.5):** The Greek *anethematisen* is the *herem* — the total destruction devoted to God — the same term used for Jericho in Joshua 6. All translators must recognize this. LOGOS correctly renders it "put them under the ban."

**On vv.62 — "not of the seed/stock of the men through whose hands salvation had been given":** This is a cutting theological verdict. Joseph and Azariah lost because they lacked the divine commission that made the Maccabees victorious — they were volunteers acting on ambition, not called leaders. The phrase echoes the theology of the Judges cycle: God works through designated deliverers.

**On the place names:** The geography of Gilead and northern Transjordan is complex. All translators preserve the place names as found in the Greek. No emendation.

---

1. When the surrounding Gentiles heard that the altar had been rebuilt and the sanctuary rededicated as before, they were greatly enraged.
2. They plotted to destroy the descendants of Jacob who lived among them and began a campaign of slaughter against the people.
3. Judas made war against the Idumeans in Akrabattene, because they were harassing Israel. He struck them a great blow, humbled them, and took their plunder.
4. He also called to mind the malice of the sons of Baean, who had been a trap and a snare to the people, lying in wait for them on the roads.
5. He besieged them in their towers, encamped against them, put them under the ban of destruction, and burned their towers with fire along with all who were inside.
6. Then he crossed over into the territory of the Ammonites, where he found a large and powerful force with Timothy at their head.
7. He fought many battles against them; they were routed before him, and he crushed them.
8. He seized Jazer and its dependent villages, then turned back toward Judea.
9. Meanwhile the Gentiles in Gilead had gathered against the Israelites who lived on their borders to destroy them; those Israelites fled to the fortified stronghold of Dathema.
10. They sent a letter to Judas and his brothers: "The Gentiles around us have gathered against us to destroy us.
11. They are preparing to come and seize the stronghold to which we have fled, and Timothy is leading their forces.
12. Come now and rescue us from their hands, for many of us have already fallen.
13. All our kindred in the land of Tobias have been killed; the enemy has led away their wives and children and seized their possessions, destroying about a thousand souls there."
14. While they were still reading the letter, other messengers arrived from Galilee with their garments torn, bringing a report of similar content,
15. saying: "The people of Ptolemais, Tyre, and Sidon have gathered against us, along with all the Galilee of the Gentiles, to destroy us."
16. When Judas and the people heard these things, a great assembly was convened to decide what should be done for their kindred who were in distress and under attack by enemies.
17. Judas said to his brother Simon: "Choose men and go and rescue our kindred in Galilee. My brother Jonathan and I will go to Gilead."
18. He left Joseph son of Zechariah and Azariah in command of the people with the remaining forces to hold Judea;
19. and he gave them these orders: "Take charge of this people, but do not engage the Gentiles in battle until we return."
20. Three thousand men were assigned to Simon for Galilee, and eight thousand to Judas for Gilead.
21. Simon marched into Galilee and fought many battles with the Gentiles. The Gentiles were routed before him,
22. and he pursued them to the very gate of Ptolemais. About three thousand Gentiles fell; he took their plunder.
23. He gathered the Jews who were in Galilee and in Arbatta — with their wives and children and all that they had — and brought them back to Judea with great rejoicing.
24. Judas Maccabeus and his brother Jonathan crossed the Jordan and marched three days' journey through the wilderness.
25. The Nabateans met them and welcomed them peaceably, and gave them a full account of everything that had happened to their kindred in Gilead:
26. that many of them were shut up in Bosora, Bosor in Alema, Caspho, Maked, and Carnaim — all large, well-fortified cities —
27. and that others were confined in the remaining cities of Gilead, and that the enemy planned on the following day to attack the strongholds and seize them and destroy all the men in a single day.
28. At once Judas turned his army and struck Bosora through the desert road. He took the city, put all the men to the sword, seized all the plunder, and burned the city.
29. They set out by night and traveled until they came to the stronghold.
30. At dawn, when they looked up, they saw an enormous force — beyond counting — carrying ladders and siege engines to take the stronghold; and already the fighting was underway.
31. Judas saw that the battle had been joined and that the cries of the city were rising to heaven along with trumpet blasts and a great tumult.
32. He said to his men: "Fight today for your kindred!"
33. He led three columns in a charge against the enemy's rear, sounding the trumpets and crying out in prayer.
34. When the army of Timothy recognized that it was Maccabeus, they fled before him. He struck them a great blow; about eight thousand of them fell that day.
35. He turned against Maspha, attacked it, took it, killed all the men, seized the plunder, and burned it.
36. From there he marched and took Caspho, Maked, Bosor, and the other cities of Gilead.
37. After these events Timothy assembled another army and encamped opposite Raphon, on the far side of the ravine.
38. Judas sent men to reconnoiter the army; they returned with their report: "All the surrounding nations have gathered to him — a very large force.
39. They have also hired Arab auxiliaries; they are camped on the far side of the ravine, ready to come against you in battle." And Judas went to meet them.
40. Timothy said to the commanders of his force: "If Judas crosses the ravine first to engage us, we will not be able to withstand him — he will certainly overpower us.
41. But if he holds back and camps on the far side, we will cross over and overpower him."
42. As Judas approached the ravine, he posted the officers of the army at the bank and gave this order: "Do not let anyone hold back; all must advance to the battle."
43. He himself crossed first, and all the people followed. The Gentiles were routed before them, threw down their weapons, and fled to the temple precinct at Carnaim.
44. They took the city and burned the temple precinct with all who were in it. Carnaim was subdued and could not hold out against Judas.
45. Judas mustered all the Israelites who were in Gilead — young and old, with their wives and children and all their belongings — a very great company — to journey to the land of Judah.
46. They came to Ephron, a large city lying squarely across their path, powerfully fortified; there was no way to bypass it, to the right or the left — they had to pass through it.
47. The townspeople locked them out and barricaded the gates with stones.
48. Judas sent them a message of peace: "Let us pass through your land to reach our own land. No one will harm you; we will simply pass through on foot." But they refused to open.
49. Judas then gave the order throughout the camp for all to halt and encamp where they stood.
50. The soldiers encamped and fought against the city all that day and all that night; and the city fell into his hands.
51. He put all the males to the sword, razed the city to its foundations, seized the plunder, and passed through the city over the bodies of the slain.
52. They crossed the Jordan into the great plain facing Beth-shan.
53. Throughout the march Judas kept gathering the stragglers and encouraging the people, until they reached the land of Judah.
54. They went up to Mount Zion with joy and gladness and offered burnt offerings, because not one of them had fallen before they returned home safely.
55. Now in the days when Judas and Jonathan were in Gilead and Simon his brother was in Galilee before Ptolemais,
56. Joseph son of Zechariah and Azariah, commanders of the forces, heard reports of the brave deeds and the battles the others had won.
57. They said: "Let us also make a name for ourselves — let us go out and fight the Gentiles around us."
58. They issued orders to the men under their command and marched toward Jamnia.
59. But Gorgias and his men came out of the city to meet them in battle.
60. Joseph and Azariah were routed and pursued to the borders of Judea. About two thousand Israelites fell that day.
61. It was a great defeat for the people, because they had not listened to Judas and his brothers and had gone out on their own initiative.
62. They were not of the stock of those men through whose hands deliverance had been given to Israel.
63. The man Judas and his brothers were greatly honored throughout all Israel and among all the Gentiles wherever their name became known.
64. People thronged to them and praised them.
65. Judas marched with his brothers against the Idumeans in the Negeb. He struck Hebron and its surrounding villages, tore down its strongholds, and burned the towers around it.
66. He moved camp and marched into Philistine territory, passing through Marissa.
67. On that day some priests who were eager to win honor fell in battle — they had gone out to fight without authorization.
68. Judas turned aside toward Azotus in Philistine territory; he tore down their altars, burned the carved images of their gods, plundered the cities, and returned to the land of Judah.
